items.title: Contro la violenza sulle donne oltre diecimila bar per la prevenzione
items.summary: Al via da Milano il progetto nazionale di Illycaffè e Arma dei Carabinieri
items.content: Trasformare oltre diecimila bar in tutta Italia in luoghi di informazione, sensibilizzazione e prevenzione della violenza sulle donne, aiutando i cittadini a riconoscere i segnali che possono precedere le forme più gravi di violenza e facendo conoscere alle vittime gli strumenti di tutela e i percorsi di sostegno a loro disposizione. È l'obiettivo del progetto nazionale promosso da Illycaffè e dall'Arma dei Carabinieri, che ha preso il via a Milano, in occasione della Giornata internazionale per l'eliminazione della violenza contro le donne, con un incontro aperto al pubblico al ristorante Voce Aimo e Nadia, alla presenza dell'amministratrice delegata di Illycaffè, Cristina Scocchia, del generale di brigata Rodolfo Santovito, comandante provinciale dei Carabinieri di Milano, e di rappresentanti dei centri antiviolenza. L'iniziativa si inserisce nell'ambito del protocollo d'intesa triennale sottoscritto il primo ottobre da Illycaffè e dal Comando generale dell'Arma dei Carabinieri, che prevede una serie di attività divulgative per promuovere la cultura della legalità e la sicurezza dei cittadini. "Ho voluto fortemente questo incontro e questa collaborazione con l'Arma dei Carabinieri perché ritengo che il silenzio e l'indifferenza siano i principali complici della violenza", ha spiegato Scocchia. "La violenza di genere non è solo un dramma privato, è anche una questione sociale e culturale e come tale riguarda tutti. Tutti abbiamo la responsabilità di contribuire a risolverla". L'accordo prevede il coinvolgimento della rete di esercizi commerciali che servono il caffè dell'azienda triestina, sfruttando la capillarità di luoghi di aggregazione frequentati quotidianamente dai cittadini per diffondere una maggiore consapevolezza del fenomeno. "Abbiamo firmato un accordo triennale con l'Arma per mettere a disposizione oltre diecimila bar che servono il nostro caffè - ha aggiunto Scocchia - perché questi possano diventare luoghi di sensibilizzazione e di prevenzione attraverso il materiale informativo che svilupperemo con l'Arma e distribuiremo proprio nei nostri bar". Al centro del progetto c'è il riconoscimento dei "reati spia", quelle condotte che possono rappresentare il preludio a forme di violenza più gravi, ma anche la diffusione delle informazioni sulle possibilità di chiedere aiuto e accedere ai percorsi di protezione. "Il tema della violenza contro le donne è cruciale e ci vede impegnati in prima linea tutti i giorni", ha sottolineato Santovito. "La sicurezza, soprattutto se interpretata in chiave moderna, non può essere affidata solo alla risposta repressiva, ma richiede collaborazioni e sinergie tra attori sociali e istituzionali". L'appuntamento milanese rappresenta il primo passo di un programma destinato a svilupparsi su scala nazionale. L'obiettivo, per Santovito, è che "il territorio e le istituzioni si muovano per informare il cittadino e agire in chiave preventiva e culturale, con lo spirito di impedire che i reati vengano commessi".

items.title: Le immagini di Dimorphos dopo l’impatto di DART
items.summary: Le immagini di Dimorphos dopo l’impatto di DART
items.content:
Dimorphos, il piccolo asteroide la cui orbita attorno a un corpo più grande è stata deviata dall'impatto di una sonda spaziale nel 202, la sonda DARTY, ha oggi una faccia appiattita da un cratere grande quanto uno stadio e ruota in modo caotico. Intorno alla coppia binaria, nel frattempo, si muovono centinaia di massi finora ignoti.
Sono le prime rivelazioni della missione Hera dell'ESA a cui partecipano ASI e ricercatori del Politecnico di Milano, che sta osservando da vicino il sistema formato da Dimorphos, una piccola luna di 151 metri di diametro, e dall'asteroide Didymos, di 730 metri, attorno al quale orbita. La coppia percorre la propria orbita solare e si trova attualmente a 193,5 milioni di chilometri dalla Terra.. L'impatto che ha cambiato un asteroide
Dimorphos è entrato nei libri di storia il 26 settembre 2022, quando la sonda DART della NASA lo ha colpito deliberatamente, accorciandone l'orbita di ben 33 minuti, molto più di quanto previsto. Mentre i telescopi sulla Terra misuravano il cambiamento orbitale, restava però aperta una domanda fondamentale: che cosa era successo davvero all'asteroide?
«Gli scienziati hanno discusso se Dimorphos avesse subito la formazione di un cratere da impatto, se avesse cambiato forma o se fosse rimasto lo stesso», spiega Patrick Michel, ricercatore principale della missione Hera e direttore di ricerca al CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur. «Con nostra grande sorpresa, la risposta si è rivelata essere tutte e tre le cose contemporaneamente. La faccia colpita da DART è stata appiattita formando un cratere da impatto delle dimensioni di uno stadio sportivo, che si estende per l'intera larghezza dell'asteroide».. Il resto della superficie, invece, non mostra segni di cambiamenti significativi: i campi di massi che ricoprono le altre regioni appaiono esattamente come nelle immagini di DART del 2022. Con l'arrivo di nuove immagini è emerso un altro dato: «L'impatto di DART ha fatto sì che Dimorphos ruotasse in modo incontrollato nella sua orbita», afferma Michael Kueppers, scienziato della missione Hera dell'ESA.. Una nuvola di massi in orbita
La seconda sorpresa riguarda l'ambiente che circonda i due asteroidi. Secondo Kueppers, Hera sta mostrando come siano circondati da centinaia di massi in orbita, di dimensioni di appena pochi metri. Il team dovrà tenerne conto nelle prossime settimane, man mano che la sonda si avvicinerà per acquisire immagini ad alta risoluzione.. Da Berlino, tra i dinosauri
A svelare le prime immagini è stato il responsabile della missione, Ian Carnelli, dalla sala dei dinosauri del Museum für Naturkunde di Berlino. «Sessantasei milioni di anni fa, l'impatto di un asteroide ha cambiato il corso della vita sulla Terra. Oggi, per la prima volta nella storia, l'umanità sta verificando come impedire che un evento del genere si ripeta», ha ricordato Carnelli.. «La missione DART della NASA ha dimostrato che possiamo modificare l'orbita di un asteroide. Hera sta ora rivelando cosa è successo all'asteroide stesso. Combinando queste due missioni, l'umanità sta compiendo un passo decisivo verso la trasformazione della deviazione degli asteroidi in uno strumento affidabile per proteggere il nostro pianeta».. Cooperazione internazionale
Per il direttore generale dell'ESA Josef Aschbacher si tratta di «collaborazione internazionale al suo meglio»: dopo che la NASA ha dimostrato che un asteroide può essere deviato, l'ESA fornisce ora l'analisi scientifica dettagliata necessaria per capire come abbia funzionato la deviazione, con preziosi contributi di partner internazionali, tra cui l'agenzia spaziale giapponese JAXA. «Insieme, stiamo trasformando un esperimento riuscito nelle conoscenze scientifiche necessarie per sviluppare una capacità affidabile di difesa planetaria», aggiunge Aschbacher. «Hera dimostra il contributo dell'Europa a uno sforzo che, in ultima analisi, va a beneficio di tutta l'umanità».. La sonda e i suoi strumenti
Hera, grande quanto un'utilitaria, ha condotto le osservazioni con tre strumenti: la fotocamera monocromatica Asteroid Framing Camera, lo spettrometro multispettrale Hyperscout-H, capace di osservare contemporaneamente in 25 colori distinti, e la termocamera a infrarossi TIRI della JAXA, che misura le temperature superficiali.
Il veicolo vola a una distanza di circa 30-25 chilometri da Didymos e Dimorphos e usa i propri propulsori per mantenere «orbite rettangolari» attorno ai due corpi a gravità ultra-bassa, a una velocità media di appena 12 centimetri al secondo.. Prossime tappe: avvicinamento e CubeSat
Queste prime immagini, precisa l'ESA, segnano l'inizio e non la conclusione dell'indagine. A dicembre la sonda dovrebbe avvicinarsi fino a circa 13 chilometri dalla coppia, con immagini a risoluzione progressivamente più alta. Nel gennaio 2027 Hera prevede di lanciare due CubeSat grandi come una scatola da scarpe, che si spingeranno ancora più vicino.
Il primo, Juventas, guidato dal Lussemburgo, userà un radar a bassa frequenza per sondare per la prima volta l'interno di un asteroide e tenterà infine un atterraggio. Il secondo, Milani, guidato dall'Italia, analizzerà i materiali dell'asteroide e la polvere circostante. . «Oggi abbiamo avuto un'ulteriore conferma che il test di deviazione dell'asteroide Dimorphos è avvenuto con successo - ha dichiarato Francesco Topputo, responsabile per l'analisi di missione e il sistema di guida e navigazione di "Milani" - Nelle prossime settimane lavoreremo al rilascio del CubeSat Milani che ci permetterà di acquisire ulteriori dettagli». Milani e Juventas, insieme a Hera, formeranno un sistema di esplorazione pionieristico: tre veicoli spaziali attorno a due asteroidi, con misurazioni complementari delle loro proprietà fisiche e delle conseguenze dell'impatto di DART.
Di particolare importanza sarà la determinazione della massa di Dimorphos. Combinata con la variazione del moto orbitale misurata da DART, aiuterà gli scienziati a quantificare l'efficacia dell'impatto e a migliorare i modelli usati per prevedere come altri asteroidi potrebbero reagire a tentativi di deviazione. Hera e i suoi CubeSat sono stati realizzati da un consorzio di 18 Stati membri dell'ESA, guidato da OHB in Germania.. Dopo Hera, Ramses
Hera è la prima missione di difesa planetaria dell'ESA, ma solo l'inizio delle ambizioni europee in questo campo. L'agenzia sta sviluppando con la JAXA anche Ramses, destinata a studiare l'asteroide Apophis durante il suo passaggio eccezionalmente ravvicinato, ma del tutto sicuro, vicino alla Terra, previsto per venerdì 13 aprile 2029. Passando a circa 32.000 chilometri sopra la superficie terrestre, Apophis subirà forze gravitazionali che potrebbero alterarne rotazione, superficie o struttura interna. Ramses osserverà questi effetti da vicino, offrendo una rara occasione per capire come un asteroide reagisca a un incontro ravvicinato con un pianeta.
Con le immagini di Dimorphos, il primo esperimento di deviazione di un asteroide realizzato dall'umanità entra nella sua fase più importante: capire non solo che la tecnica funziona, ma anche perché, e in quali condizioni ci si potrà fare affidamento in futuro..

items.title: Guinea orders residents to clean up the capital months after deadly rubbish dump collapse
items.summary: The capital's main rubbish dump has been closed since the disaster, leading to rubbish piling up in the streets.
items.content:
Guinea has ordered residents to do a mass clean-up of the capital, Conakry, months after a rubbish landfill collapsed, killing dozens of people.

Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday announced a deadline of 31 December to clear rubbish in the city and its suburbs, which has seen an increase in illegal dumping in recent months.

In August heavy rains caused a landslide at the capital's main waste dump, with the rubbish collapsing onto homes killing 31 people and injuring others.

The site in the city's Dar es Salaam area was subsequently closed permanently, which has led to piles of rubbish accumulating outside homes and on the streets.

At a public forum on sanitation, Sanitation Minister Aboubacar Camara said Conakry was generating about 3,000 tonnes of waste every day.

He said much of the garbage was ending up in the streets because of weaknesses in the collection system.

The prime minister called on local authorities to become more involved in organising waste collection, saying this could become a way to create jobs.

"The state will do its part, but the municipalities must also organise themselves to ensure waste collection and provide jobs for young people," the prime minister said.

"Conakry must be completely clean by the end of December," he added, relaying a directive from the country's president, Mamady Doumbouya.

He cited measures the government was taking to improve waste collection and recycling, including a national sanitation fund that would guarantee financing for the sector.

Camara said talks had been finalised with a waste collection operator, with a plan for equipment to move waste from transit and sorting centres to a new disposal site in Baretodé, outside the capital.

The August tragedy at the Dar es Salaam landfill was not the first - 10 people were killed at the same site in 2017.

The government had ordered people living close to the site to move, but many residents chose to stay.

According to the prime minister, the government now plans to transform the closed waste site into an urban park.

items.title: C’è una seconda puntata dell’inchiesta sulle frasi antisemite attribuite a Jordan Bardella
items.summary: “Le Monde” ha pubblicato nuovi messaggi del 2013, con tirate contro le banche e la finanza
items.content:
Le Monde , il principale quotidiano francese, ha pubblicato una nuova inchiesta sui messaggi antisemiti attribuiti a Jordan Bardella , il presidente del partito di estrema destra Rassemblement National, che con Marine Le Pen è favorito alle elezioni presidenziali del prossimo aprile.

È basata sullo stesso materiale di una precedente inchiesta del sito Mediapart , uscita a fine settembre e che fece molto clamore in Francia. I messaggi risalgono al 2013, quindi al periodo iniziale della carriera politica di Bardella, che aveva poco più di 18 anni (oggi ne ha 31).

Sono messaggi mandati su Facebook Messenger: L e Monde scrive di averne verificato l’autenticità con Meta (l’azienda proprietaria di Facebook) e di aver intervistato la persona a cui erano destinati, che per la prima volta ha dato informazioni sul loro contesto. Le Monde chiama questa persona “Sacha”, un nome di fantasia.

Il Rassemblement National è stato più volte criticato per le dichiarazioni antisemite, passate e presenti, fatte da alcuni dei suoi funzionari e candidati alle elezioni . Da qualche anno il partito sta provando a cambiare immagine , presentandosi tra le altre cose come un protettore dei francesi di fede ebraica. I messaggi cozzano anche con l’immagine di Bardella, che ha coltivato legami col mondo imprenditoriale e affaristico in preparazione alla probabile successione a Le Pen, storica leader del partito.

Molti dei messaggi sono tirate contro le banche e la finanza, accusate di essere colluse o controllate da un presunto circolo di persone ebree. Sacha ha detto a Le Monde che Bardella «anche quando parlavamo di politica internazionale o economia, tutto lo riportava sempre agli ebrei. Era un’ossessione. Era parte del suo quadro politico».

I leader del Rassemblement National Jordan Bardella e Marine Le Pen durante una conferenza stampa a Parigi, il 17 novembre (AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard)

Ai tempi Bardella era un attivista del Front National (il precedente nome del Rassemblement) del Seine-Saint-Denis, il dipartimento a nord di Parigi dove Bardella è nato e cresciuto. Lui e Sacha frequentavano la stessa scuola privata cattolica, la Jean-Baptiste de La Salle. Sacha ha detto che, da quando Bardella aveva capito che gli interessava la politica, cercava di convincerlo a unirsi a lui.

Vari scambi tra i due sono intrisi di cospirazionismo. Nei messaggi si suggerisce di non fidarsi dei media, perché sarebbero controllati da un’élite economica con legami con persone ebree. «Sono i sionisti che sono a capo delle banche; non è un caso che Attali [l’economista Jacques Attali] sia a favore di un nuovo ordine mondiale con Gerusalemme per capitale, per esempio; tutto è connesso», dice un messaggio a Sacha, che poi invita a dirgli i capi delle principali banche mondiali. (Attali è un economista e intellettuale francese che ha avuto ruoli tecnici in vari governi e istituzioni europee tra gli anni Ottanta e gli anni Duemila. È nato in Algeria e suo padre era ebreo).

Come detto, i passaggi sono in contraddizione con l’approccio pro business del Bardella adulto. Per esempio, uno riassume il sostegno a Le Pen sottolineando questi punti: «Riprendere il controllo delle banche, protezionismo economico, svalutazione della moneta… aggiungerei l’antisionismo ^^» (gli ultimi due caratteri sono probabilmente una faccina sorridente). Oppure: «Sono le banche che comandano; i politici sono lì per fare il lavoro sporco».

items.title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold
items.summary: Indonesian authorities say another 13 are missing in the illegal gold mine, which flooded on Monday.
items.content:
It's been three days since Rani last saw her father as he left for work on Monday. Early on Tuesday, she received news that he was trapped underground.

Rais, 50, had been working as an illegal gold miner in Bogor, Indonesia's West Java province. On Monday night, he and at least 25 other miners were digging in an open-pit mine about 100m (328ft) deep, when torrential rain caused a nearby river to overflow and flood the two shafts.

Authorities on Thursday confirmed that 13 people had died and their bodies were recovered from the site. At least 13 more are thought to still be missing.

Search-and-rescue operations are ongoing, with personnel using ropes to access the depths of the dark, narrow and slippery mine shafts, which are continually being flooded from below.

Above ground, ambulances and medical personnel are ready and waiting to transport victims.

"We are coordinating with all search and rescue personnel involved in the operation to monitor water conditions and assess access to the mine shaft," Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The depth of the shaft, narrow access and limited lighting are key considerations in determining the search strategy so that personnel can operate safely."

Small-scale gold mining is banned in Indonesia, but remains widespread in rural parts of the mineral-rich archipelago.

Multiple studies show that over the past ten years the illegal industry has rapidly flourished, often in correlation with rising gold prices. In early 2026, those prices reached an all-time high – spurring a gold rush that prompted mine operators across the country to expand their operations.

This included state-owned mining company Aneka Tambang (Antam), which owns the business permit for the area in which this week's flooded mine is located. Antam have said the mine was not theirs and was operating without their authorisation.

On Wednesday, while rescue operations there were underway, West Java Regional Police separately announced that they had uncovered 24 cases of illegal mining across the province between October and November alone.

But Bisman Bakhtiar, Executive Director of the Center for Energy and Mining Law Studies, told the BBC earlier this year that the actual number of illegal mines in Indonesia is higher than the government's figures.

"[The government figures are] what's been recorded. That means there must be more than that," he said, noting that law enforcement operations have had little impact on the sector.

"It's still very massive and very big because this has been going on for a very long time."

Others allege that the illegal industry is underpinned by corruption.

Laode M Syarif, former deputy chairman of the Corruption Eradication Committee, said that unofficial mining is difficult to eradicate because every illegal mine has "backing", usually from "police and military or high-ranking officials in local and provincial governments".

"As long as these backers are not dealt with firmly, illegal mining will continue," he said.

In many cases, though, the allure of these mines is simple: they offer an economic lifeline to people with few other viable prospects.

Despite the value of gold having dipped in recent months, countless illegal miners throughout Indonesia are still eagerly digging for paydirt.

But the lack of regulation and poor construction in the pits also means accidents are relatively common – whether from landslides, floods, or exposure to hazardous gases, all of which have claimed lives in recent years.

Earlier this year, in the same area as this week's flooded mine, 11 illegal gold miners reportedly died after a carbon monoxide leak inside a shaft.

Elsewhere, in West Sumatra, nine people were killed at an illegal gold mine in May after heavy rain triggered the collapse of a 30-metre cliff, burying 12 miners in total.

There are numerous reports of other such incidents across the Indonesian archipelago. But the illegal nature of the small-scale gold mining sector obfuscates the true number of casualties.

Even this week, when asked how many miners were in the pits in Bogor when they flooded, M Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor Regency Regional Disaster Management Agency, said the total casualty figure "is still unclear".

"Some say 20 people, others say 29 people," Hamdani told Indonesian news outlet Detik. "The problem is that no one reported it and no one wants to report it."

The Indonesian Ombudsman on Thursday urged law enforcement officials to conduct a thorough investigation of the incident and to address the larger systemic issue behind it.

"This should be a momentum for all parties to resolve the [illegal gold mining] problem comprehensively, not just taking action after the incident or closing the holes discovered," said Abdul Ghoffar, a member of the Indonesian Ombudsman.

"We need to uncover the entire [illegal gold mining] chain," he continued. "We must not allow only the miners in the field to be seen and prosecuted, while those who control the activities, provide capital and facilities, store, and market the mined products remain untouched.

"Law enforcement must target the actors and networks that keep this illegal activity going."

As rescue operations continue and more bodies are recovered, the picture is becoming less murky. But even if there are survivors among those who remain missing, time may be running out.

More than three days since the shafts flooded, the relatives of the anonymous men in the mines are desperately waiting to hear whether their loved ones survived.

As she waits for news of her father, Rani says: "I hope he's found soon."

items.title: Per la prima volta nella sua storia la parata del Ringraziamento di Macy’s a New York è stata posticipata per maltempo
items.content:
Da più di 100 anni nel giorno del Ringraziamento decine di carri con palloni aerostatici che raffigurano personaggi dei cartoni animati e dei fumetti sfilano per le strade di Manhattan, in centro a New York: quest’anno non sarà così. La parata è famosa in tutto il mondo come Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade , organizzata dai grandi magazzini Macy’s per aprire la stagione dello shopping prima delle feste natalizie, ma quest’anno è stata posticipata a causa del maltempo.

Giovedì a New York sono previsti venti molto forti e piogge molto intense e il sindaco Zohran Mamdani ha detto che potrebbero esserci anche improvvisi allagamenti. L’azienda ha quindi fatto sapere che la parata sarà posticipata a sabato. È la prima volta che la parata viene posticipata dal 1924, l’anno della prima edizione. Era stata sospesa solo tra il 1942 e il 1944, durante la seconda guerra mondiale.

Il rinvio della parata richiede un enorme riassetto logistico che sta coinvolgendo le forze dell’ordine cittadine e vari dipartimenti del comune, oltre ai dipendenti e ai volontari di Macy’s. I palloni sono stati sgonfiati mercoledì e riportati in un magazzino in New Jersey, e saranno riportati a New York venerdì e rigonfiati nel pomeriggio.

items.title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats
items.summary: Gen Kainerugaba threatened a rebel takeover of a mineral-rich area in DR Congo in controversial X posts.
items.content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the president's son.

In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo. He insisted that Uganda's military involvement was purely driven by security concerns.

The DR Congo's foreign ministry summoned Uganda's envoy to explain the remarks, describing them as "particularly serious" and damaging to diplomatic relations.

The diplomatic row comes despite close military ties between the neighbours.

Their forces have been conducting joint operations against the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern DR Congo since 2021.

Uganda has also recently been involved in efforts to mediate between the Congolese government and an armed group led by former warlord Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province.

Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever

In his posts, Gen Kainerugaba accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), an armed group operating in eastern DR Congo, of targeting members of the Bahima ethnic community.

The Bahema are a traditionally cattle-herding community mainly based in DR Congo's north-eastern Ituri province.

They have historical and cultural ties to the Bahima people of neighbouring Uganda.

He also threatened a rebel takeover of Walikale, in North Kivu province, while defending Uganda's military presence in DR Congo.

Walikale is rich in mineral resources , including some of the country's largest tin deposits and several major gold mines.

Gen Kainerugaba's X account, which had nearly 1.4 million followers, has since become inaccessible.

It is unclear whether he deactivated it, as he has done in the past, or whether the platform had suspended it.

During the same week he declared: "My tweets in Uganda are directives that must be obeyed."

The posts followed reports that a DR Congo military aircraft had allegedly been shot down by rebels , with foreign mercenaries reportedly among those on board.

Gen Kainerugaba criticised the reported presence of foreign mercenaries in DR Congo.

"These remarks, which are particularly serious, have caused a major media incident and undermine the necessary restraint that must prevail in relations between sovereign states," the DR Congo foreign ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The Congolese government expects the Republic of Uganda to clarify its official position and take the necessary measures to prevent such transgressions from recurring in the future".

The ministry added that DR Congo remained committed to regional peace and stability but would defend its dignity and institutions against "any form of provocation or interference".

It is not the first time Gen Kainerugaba's social media posts have strained relations between the two countries.

In February last year, he threatened to seize the eastern DR Congo city of Bunia, claiming that members of the Bahima ethnic community were being attacked.

In 2024, DR Congo also summoned Uganda's diplomatic representative after the general made threats against foreign mercenaries operating in eastern DR Congo.

The 52-year-old general, widely seen as a potential successor to his father Yoweri Museveni, has become known for his provocative social media posts.

In 2022, he sparked a diplomatic row with neighbouring Kenya after threatening to invade the country and capture its capital, Nairobi, prompting his father to apologise forn the remarks.

items.title: Il testo della lettera di Gianni De Gennaro
items.summary: In cui si difende dalle accuse senza fare grandi rivelazioni: l'ha pubblicato il Corriere della Sera
items.content:
Il Corriere della Sera ha pubblicato alcune parti di una lettera scritta dall’ex capo della polizia Gianni De Gennaro il giorno prima di uccidersi , lo scorso 21 novembre. Subito dopo la morte si era saputo di due lettere trovate vicino al corpo di De Gennaro, una indirizzata ai familiari e l’altra «a chi vorrà pubblicarla», di conseguenza c’era grande attesa di conoscerne il contenuto. Ma la lettera non contiene grandi rivelazioni, è più che altro la versione dei fatti di De Gennaro e una difesa di se stesso dalle accuse della procura di Caltanissetta che lo stava indagando per il depistaggio delle indagini sulla strage di via D’Amelio del 1992, a Palermo, in cui furono uccisi il giudice Paolo Borsellino e cinque agenti della sua scorta.

Una parte della lettera è dedicata alle scuse verso alcune persone della sua vita che sono state coinvolte dalle indagini a suo carico , inclusi i familiari. Lui la definisce il suo «testamento morale».

Assieme alla lettera ha lasciato anche un hard disk su cui ha detto di aver archiviato tutti i documenti che dovrebbero rispondere alle domande di chi indaga sui casi in cui era coinvolto.

«Fra qualche minuto non ci sarò più e quindi capite bene che un “condannato a morte” non può mentire», scrive De Gennaro all’inizio della lettera, riportata dai giornalisti del Corriere della Sera Fiorenza Sarzanini e Giovanni Bianconi. Il testo è indirizzato «a chi di competenza, con l’auspicio che abbia l’onestà di renderlo pubblico». È composto da otto fogli «riempiti con grafia rotonda e chiara», scrivono Sarzanini e Bianconi, che in otto pagine hanno trovato un solo refuso («Ho obbedi sempre agli ordini che mi sono stati impartiti ed ho assolto ai compiti che mi sono stati affidati, anche contro la mia volontà, con impegno») e nessuna cancellatura.

Riguardo all’hard disk, De Gennaro scrive: «Qui c’è l’oggetto dei desideri, l’hard disk che tutti cercano», riferendosi a quando era stata perquisita la sua casa romana proprio in cerca di documenti personali. «Non contiene misteri, né segreti, contiene solo i riscontri di circa 40 anni di quella che è stata parte della mia vita, fatta di sofferenze e amarezze. Esaminatelo con cura, ma con animo sereno, scevro da inutili dietrologie».

E poi aggiunge, spiegando la ragione per cui l’ha consegnato in punto di morte: «Ho solo cercato di evitare che fosse acquisito da chi non ritenevo in grado di valutarne il contenuto». I documenti dell’hard disk erano stati per anni in formato cartaceo, poi De Gennaro decise di digitalizzarli per praticità, senza però liberarsi del tutto dell’archivio cartaceo, e «coinvolgendo stupidamente un amico a cui voglio bene». Sarzanini e Bianconi ipotizzano che si tratti di un «addetto alla sua tutela che lo segue da decenni», ora indagato dalla procura di Caltanissetta con l’accusa di aver «occultato e custodito in formato digitale, su disposizione di De Gennaro, documentazione ritenuta compromettente».

Oltre a questa lettera ce n’era un’altra indirizzata ai suoi familiari. Entrambe sono state sequestrate dalla procura di Grosseto, che ha aperto un’indagine per istigazione al suicidio. Chi indaga vuole capire, in particolare, se De Gennaro abbia incontrato o parlato con qualcuno prima di uccidersi, anche se è un’eventualità considerata remota. Il primo dicembre si sarebbe dovuta tenere un’udienza al tribunale del Riesame, che avrebbe dovuto decidere sulla richiesta di arresti domiciliari avanzata dalla procura di Caltanissetta, e rigettata dal giudice per le indagini preliminari.

L’ipotesi dell’accusa contro De Gennaro era che i presunti depistaggi fossero motivati dal tentativo di evitare che emergessero elementi contro di lui su alcune vicende dell’epoca, compresa la gestione delle indagini sulle stragi di mafia del 1992.

items.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
items.summary: Female protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, a rights group says.
items.content:
In recent weeks, the 21-year-old has been unable to walk properly after her legs were beaten, and an ear-infection caused by an untreated head injury has affected her balance, her cousin says.

She is "keeping her spirits up" but "there are days she breaks down in tears," Masoud Nourmohammadi tells BBC News Persian.

He says Taraneh and her twin sister Romina were arrested after joining the anti-government protests that swept the country in January.

When the twins' mother first saw them in prison, their faces were so swollen and bruised, and their hair pulled out, that she could only recognise them by their voices, Nourmohammadi says, speaking from the US.

He says Taraneh signed a confession after interrogators threatened that her sister would be raped in front of her.

Taraneh is one of six women who have been sentenced to death this year in connection with the January protests, according to the UN's human rights rapporteur for Iran, Mai Sato.

The figure for men is much higher. However, women protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, as part of a "horrific rise" in politically motivated executions, Amnesty International's Iran researcher Raha Bahreini says.

The Iranian embassy in London told the BBC that claims of an increase in the use of the death penalty in protest-related cases were "misleading".

It categorically rejected allegations of the use of torture and any allegations that the death penalty has been imposed solely for peaceful protest, which it said is a "legitimate, and protected right".

It said death sentences in relation to the "riot in January 2026" were issued in cases involving "intentional murder" or "Moharebeh (the taking up of weapons with the intent to threaten or wreck the people's lives or property)".

It was two weeks after the end of the protests, which began in late December over economic grievances and grew to become Iran's largest against the clerical establishment since the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (Hrana) says it has identified more than 7,000 people killed in the crackdown that followed, most of them protesters, but believes the true figure is much higher.

The Iranian government accuses the US and Israel of fomenting the unrest, blaming "terrorists" and "rioters" for the deaths, which it says totalled 3,117 including some members of the security forces.

The twins' family did not find out where they were being held for more than three months, their cousin says. They were tried over protests in Isfahan, in an area of the city where a member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) security force was killed.

Court documents have not been published, but the BBC has seen part of a sentencing document which says Taraneh was convicted of moharebeh, which is a capital offence under Iran's Islamic Penal Code. The offence included "drawing a bladed weapon with the intent to endanger people's lives", according to the document.

Romina was sentenced to 25 years in jail for the lesser charge of aiding and abetting moharebeh, according to Sato, the UN rapporteur.

Nourmohammadi, who has been in contact with relatives and others in Iran familiar with the case, says both women deny all the charges against them and that there is no evidence Taraneh had a "bladed weapon".

Sato says the sisters were part of a case in which 10 people were sentenced to death, but that there was "no clarification of the acts attributed to each individual".

According to sources familiar with the case, the twins' lawyers have submitted a complaint alleging they were tortured and sexually abused during interrogation, but the investigation into it is being overseen by an official they accuse of torture.

Voice messages from other women on death row contain a mixture of desperation and defiance.

Mahboubeh Shabani - widely reported to be 33 and a civil engineer - was sentenced to death in September under Iran's espionage law after transporting injured protesters, according to rights groups.

She called for help for herself and other prisoners from jail in the city of Mashhad in north-eastern Iran: "Everyone is in a terrible place mentally, especially those whose sentences have been finalised," she said.

Also jailed in Mashhad is Najmeh Amini, reported to be 23, who was initially arrested in the wake of the January protests, and later sentenced to death after being convicted of committing blasphemy in a social media post, according to rights groups.

"As long as I am alive, I have one hope, and that is to see a free and prosperous Iran before my life ends by the noose," a voice message attributed to her says.

In addition, Mojdeh Hashemi Bazargani - reported to be aged 27 - is also facing execution, according to rights groups. They say she was convicted of charges including "espionage", after being arrested in April, during the current war between Iran and Israel and the US.

The US-based Iranian rights group Tavaana has shared audio it says is of a phone call she made from prison, describing being beaten in the head, neck and body and made to sign a confession.

The woman in the recording says: "They accused me of espionage. They say you've been paid for it. If I had been paid for espionage, I would have a car or a house. I have nothing."

Amnesty International describes the charges in all three of these cases and also the twins as "politically motivated".

In response to the BBC's questions, the Iranian Embassy in London said "any allegations of the use of torture in connection with the mentioned cases are categorically rejected". It did not comment further on individual cases, but said "confessions obtained under duress have no legal validity".

At least 39 people have already been executed in connection with the January protests, according to Sato.

She notes a "sharp" increase in arrests and sentences across both men and women, and sees the rise in death sentences for women as an "escalation and expansion" of an "established pattern of repression".

Iranian human rights lawyer Musa Barzin, who is based in Turkey, says "it appears that factors such as gender or age now carry less weight in determining the severity of punishment".

Official detail on cases is often scant and some may go unreported.

However, Sato says as well as the six women she identified as being arrested in connection with protests, a further three have received death sentences this year - for "blasphemy" and "corruption on Earth charges, in relation to the war in March" and "espionage and moharebeh".

In comparison, these nine sentences are more than Hrana recorded for women for similar offences over the whole decade to 2025 - with no more than three in any one year.

The death sentences in three of the cases Sato identified as being linked to the protests have since been overturned – though two of those have been sent for retrial. She says she is concerned by an "increasingly frequent pattern" where overturned death sentences are later "reimposed by a parallel branch of the judiciary once public attention has subsided".

Sato says there was a "turning point" for women in Iran during the 2022 protests over the death of Mahsa Amini, who died in custody after being detained over an alleged breach of Iran's dress code.

Women "were at the forefront of challenging state policies and structures of control," says Sato. "Their political agency, visibility and leadership have made them targets of state repression."

The Iranian embassy said judicial proceedings in Iran are conducted in accordance with the Constitution and rule of law. It adds: "Cases involving the death penalty have included charges such as serious criminal offences, violence, terrorism, espionage, cooperation with hostile intelligence services and Moharebeh."

Iran executes more people per head of population than any other country, according to UN experts. Human rights groups say last year saw the highest number in decades.

Hrana recorded 2,003 executions in the year to October 2026. The vast majority - including 47 women - were for crimes such as murder and drug trafficking.

Nourmohammadi says the family are trying as best they can to support the twins.

Romina enjoys music and often asks relatives to play songs over the phone, he says.

Taraneh loves horses and has always wanted to set up a horse breeding centre, he says, and they tell her they plan to help her do so in the future: "That's how we try to give her hope."

items.title: Nvidia ha bloccato le spedizioni di server verso quattro paesi del sud-est asiatico
items.summary: Per impedire alle aziende cinesi di aggirare i divieti statunitensi sui chip per l'intelligenza artificiale
items.content:
La società tecnologica statunitense Nvidia ha chiesto ai suoi partner commerciali di interrompere le spedizioni di server con i suoi chip verso Malaysia, Singapore, Thailandia e Indonesia. I quattro paesi del sud-est asiatico sono sfruttati di frequente dalle aziende cinesi che cercano di aggirare le restrizioni statunitensi sull’acquisto dei processori più avanzati per l’intelligenza artificiale. Lo ha scritto il Financial Times , citando tre persone a conoscenza della decisione.

Tra le aziende che hanno ricevuto la richiesta ci sono Dell e Supermicro, che assemblano i server usando i chip di Nvidia. Non è chiaro se l’interruzione sia temporanea: Nvidia e i suoi partner stanno cercando di capire come adeguarsi alle nuove regole introdotte la settimana scorsa dal dipartimento del Commercio statunitense per impedire alle aziende cinesi di accedere indirettamente ai processori attraverso società di altri paesi.

Le nuove regole impongono ai fornitori dei paesi del sud-est asiatico di ottenere una licenza per esportare i chip più avanzati, mentre i data center esistenti hanno 90 giorni per ottenere un’autorizzazione, dimostrando che i loro clienti non comprendono soggetti sottoposti a restrizioni. Ma la mancanza di indicazioni precise su come ottenere le licenze ha creato molta incertezza.

Il governo statunitense aveva deciso queste nuove regole dopo l’ enorme scandalo di spionaggio da parte della Cina che aveva coinvolto Jensen Huang, il cofondatore e amministratore delegato di Nvidia.

Il 12 novembre Huang si era dimesso dopo che si era venuto a sapere che aveva avuto una relazione extraconiugale con una donna di nome Alice Huang sospettata di essere un’informatrice per il governo cinese e di aver contrabbandato in Cina le tecnologie statunitensi. Meno di due settimane dopo è stato però nominato di nuovo amministratore delegato dell’azienda, anche grazie alle pressioni fatte dal governo di Donald Trump sul consiglio di amministrazione di Nvidia.

items.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
items.summary: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.
items.content:
A German boat dealer is suspected of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings to the UK, in the first four months of 2026, allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

The managing director, Marvin Reuter, is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

His equipment is suspected of being linked to two fatal accidents, in which four men died.

We confronted the 35-year-old at his business, but he would not answer our questions. He said he was reporting us to the police.

items.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
items.summary: Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm.
items.content:
A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

The managing director, Marvin Reuter, is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

His equipment is suspected of being linked to two fatal accidents, in which four men died.

We confronted the 35-year-old at his business near Dortmund, but he would not answer our questions. He said he was reporting us to the police.

Reuter cannot be formally charged until extradited to France but could face jail time, if tried and convicted. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

The BBC - alongside German broadcasters WDR and NDR, newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) - and France's Le Monde newspaper - has obtained and reviewed hundreds of police, court and tax documents about the case. We have blurred images of Reuter because of German privacy rules.

Investigators, we have learned, believe they have uncovered clear, persistent links between Reuter and smuggling networks.

Evidence has been gathered through the confessions of alleged accomplices and covert jail-cell recordings of an alleged gang chief - as well as the two deadly crossing attempts.

At least 82 boats from Reuter's firm reached the English coast in just over two years to May, according to French investigations.

There are also press photos dating back five years showing the MaReBoote logo on dinghies crowded with migrants.

In 2021, Reuter told the Sun and Guardian he felt "frustrated" and "anxious" that his vessels had ended up in the hands of smugglers.

There was no suggestion, at that time, that authorities suspected him of wrongdoing as a German detective reportedly told the Sun: "This would be like if somebody buys a Mercedes and does something in another country which is wrong. The Mercedes seller can't help that."

It is not exactly clear when police suspicions were aroused.

French prosecutor Samuel Finielz would not comment on the details of the investigation but confirmed the head of a German company is currently the subject of a European Arrest Warrant.

The warrant was issued in May this year and relates to alleged offences dating back to December 2024.

While selling boats is "perfectly legal" it becomes illegal, said Finielz, "when one is fully aware that they will be used by networks involved in illegal immigration or human trafficking".

Case files we have seen say that German police had learned from UK authorities that 29% of detected crossings this year, up to the end of April, involved boats and/or engines linked to MaReBoote.

In France, five other men have already been charged as part of the investigation - an Iranian, three Iraqis and a Syrian.

In one of the two fatal incidents where Reuter's equipment is suspected to be involved, one of those who died was also Syrian.

Suliman al Husein would have just turned 20 when he died, according to a birth date listed in the files.

News reports at the time say he suffered a cardiac arrest after likely being crushed on a packed dinghy during a failed launch, west of Calais, in January 2025.

He was the first migrant to die in the English Channel that year. His body was found on the floor of the boat which, investigators allege, bore the MaReBoote logo.

The case against Reuter also stems from a chance arrest when French police pulled over a vehicle with German plates, near the northern port city of Boulogne-sur-Mer.

The BMW, which was towing a trailer, was spotted overtaking another vehicle at speed in the early hours of a morning in May this year - police records say.

Inside the car were two German nationals who - according to a subsequent search - were transporting jerry cans of fuel, a boat engine, pumps and a rolled up inflatable dinghy.

The men claimed they had been paid up to €1,000-a-time (£830) to make several, similar drops to "foreigners" on the coast, interrogation records show.

"Of course I knew that it wasn't legal," one is said to have admitted under questioning. "The money made me turn a blind eye."

Take a look at BBC Verify's UK migration tracker - the latest numbers on net migration, visas, asylum and small boats

Both men, who have since been convicted for smuggling offences, allegedly implicated Marvin Reuter as the man who had hired and paid them for this work.

Police files say both the BMW and the boat it was carrying had MaReBoote logos on them.

Marvin Reuter was arrested in Germany in May and later released, pending extradition.

On the day of his arrest, German police also seized more than 30 dinghies and 9,000 life jackets. Equipment which, we can now reveal, was allegedly linked to Reuter.

The BBC was previously granted access to see this haul, held in a police warehouse at a secret location in western Germany.

Meanwhile, further evidence has been gleaned from the bugging of a jail cell of a suspected gang chief, who is being held in pre-trial detention in France.

Recordings captured the inmate talking about buying nautical equipment from a German firm run by a man with Reuter's first name: Marvin - according to files we have seen.

The MaReBoote company address was also discovered on the alleged smuggler's phone, the case files say.

When we confronted Reuter last month at his business in the town of Werne, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, he told us to leave and drove off.

He then returned a short time later and said he was reporting us to the police. He did not answer our questions.

We approached him in writing before and after this encounter including a detailed request for comment. In response to that request, he did not address the specific allegations but accused us of harassment.

It is understood Reuter's lawyers have challenged his extradition, citing overcrowding in French prisons as one reason. Their client should face any allegations in Germany, they argue.

In Germany, it became explicitly illegal to aid smuggling to the UK at the end of last year after a prior BBC investigation exposed the country's role as a storage hub for gangs. Before then, some anti-smuggling laws in Germany had no longer applied to the UK because of Brexit.

The raid that saw the seizure of equipment that was allegedly linked to Reuter marked the first time the new law had been used.

Small boat crossings have dropped significantly in 2026, with British authorities citing law enforcement as a "key factor" . However, illegal migration into Europe has also been falling.

The UK National Crime Agency's (NCA) deputy director for organized immigration crime, Dan Cannatella-Barcroft, praised Germany's "commitment" to tackling people-smuggling but acknowledged the country would remain "an important piece of the puzzle".

While a gap in the law has been closed, Germany's proximity to France, wider transport links and the fact that some of the Kurdish-dominated gangs are based there, means it is expected to stay as a transit point in the illegal small-boats trade.

The "vast majority" of small boats equipment in the past few years has come through Germany, Cannatella-Barcroft told the BBC - much of it made in China and having been routed through Turkey.

items.title: Un unico vaccino per mangiare tranquilli
items.summary: Un unico vaccino per mangiare tranquilli
items.content:
Un unico vaccino che fornisca all'organismo le istruzioni per gestire gli allergeni potrebbe garantire pasti senza pensieri alle circa 220 milioni di persone che nel mondo convivono con allergie alimentari. Il candidato vaccino, basato sulla stessa tecnologia a mRNA dei vaccini anti-covid, ha dato risultati promettenti nei topi e potrebbe un giorno arrivare alla sperimentazione clinica. Lo descrive un articolo pubblicato su Nature Communications.. Un allergene modello per allenare gli anticorpi. Un gruppo di scienziati dell'Università Tecnica della Danimarca ha pensato di allenare il sistema immunitario a gestire gli allergeni alimentari, cioè le proteine contenute nel cibo che possono innescare nelle persone allergiche reazioni immunitarie anomale, costruendo un allergene sintetico che "riassuma" in sé le caratteristiche di un'ampia famiglia di queste sostanze.
L'allergene scelto per lo studio è modellato sulle proteine ​​di trasferimento lipidico non specifiche - nsLTP, dall'inglese non-specific Lipid Transfer Proteins - proteine molto diffuse tra specie vegetali (sono presenti, per esempio, sulla buccia dei frutti) che possono scatenare allergie crociate.. Le allergie crociate sono reazioni allergiche scatenate nella stessa persona da cause apparentemente scollegate, per esempio polline e alimenti di origine vegetale, o graminacee e pomodoro: dipendono dal fatto che le proteine che innescano la risposta immunitaria sono simili tra loro. Le nsLTP sono presenti in numerosi alimenti vegetali tipici dell'area mediterranea, come pesche, mele e noci, nel polline di olivo, platano e artemisia. . Istruzioni per l'uso. Gli scienziati hanno pensato a un vaccino a mRNA in grado di fornire al sistema immunitario non l'allergene vero e proprio, bensì le istruzioni per produrre anticorpi protettivi che sappiano riconoscere e bloccare gli allergeni di questa famiglia, quando li incontreranno. «L'idea è che se sei allergico a varie cose diverse, che condividono all'incirca la stessa struttura molecolare, si possa usare questa struttura per produrre un allergene artificiale, che a sua volta possa essere incorporato in un vaccino» spiega Esperanza Rivera de Torre, tra gli autori della ricerca.. L'obiettivo è prevenire eventuali reazioni allergiche, con un approccio (fornire le sole istruzioni e non l'allergene in sé) opposto rispetto a quello usato nelle terapie di desensibilizzazione orale, che prevedono la somministrazione di quantità progressivamente crescenti di un allergene fino a raggiungere uno stato di non reattività.. I risultati nei topi. Il vaccino, somministrato in tre dosi a distanza di tre settimane a topi sani o affetti da allergie alimentari, ha sollecitato un'importante produzione di anticorpi protettivi e fornito un'ampia protezione contro gli allergeni. Il vaccino a mRNA non ha scatenato reazioni avverse di rilievo nei topi allergici, ma non ha garantito una protezione assoluta contro lo shock anafilattico, nella concentrazione e nel numero di dosi testato.. Inoltre, gli anticorpi protettivi prodotti dai topi sono riusciti a ridurre le reazioni allergiche contro questa classe di allergeni nei campioni di sangue di pazienti allergici.. Sviluppi futuri. Lo studio è servito a dimostrare che un vaccino contro le allergie alimentari è tecnicamente fattibile, e che ha le carte in regola per essere efficace. Occorrerà però approfondire quando, e in quali quantità vada somministrato per offrire una protezione completa contro lo shock anafilattico, e rifinire l'involucro lipidico che protegge le istruzioni per attivare il sistema immunitario così da indirizzare meglio e a proprio favore le risposte immunitarie. Infine, lo stesso design potrebbe essere sfruttato per inserire nel vaccino le istruzioni per diverse classi di allergeni..

items.title: Unconditional Integer Factorization in Subexponential Time
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/4a7bc8ab0bc770e71a259b7966c500496b99010a/cogentic_research_papers/integer_factorization Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50651627 Points: 78 # Comments: 9
items.content:
This paper constructs an unconditional, zero-error Las Vegas algorithm on a single fixed uniform classical multitape Turing machine $\mathcal{M}$ that computes the exact complete prime factorization $N = \prod_{1 \le i \le k} p_i^{e_i}$ ( $p_1 < \dots < p_k$ prime, $e_i \ge 1$ ) of every integer $N \ge 2$ given in standard binary representation, halting with probability $1$ over its read-once fair coin flips, in worst-case expected time $L_N[1/3, 105]$ and worst-case deterministic workspace $L_N[1/3, 40]$ , where

$$L_x(\alpha, c) := \exp!\bigl(c,(\ln x)^\alpha (\ln\ln x)^{1-\alpha}\bigr)$$

$$ \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\ln \max(1, T(N))}{(\ln N)^\alpha (\ln\ln N)^{1-\alpha}} \le c. $$

Every prime factor in the output is certified deterministically via Agrawal–Kayal–Saxena primality testing and direct multiplication against $N$ , with effectively computable constants and no unproven number-theoretic hypotheses. A complete, unconditional, Mathlib-only Lean 4 ( v4.35.0 ) formalization of the entire proof has also been completed and will be released in a companion submission.

This paper and its Lean 4 formalization were entirely obtained by Cogentic (arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.40324 ), an agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model. There was no human interaction other than the initial prompt for Cogentic to generate a full proof and formalization. The Cogentic harness was built by Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, and Di Wang (Google Research and Google DeepMind).

items.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
items.summary: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
items.content:
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.

The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

The White House began investigating the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal .

China is facing the highest tariff rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35%, with others facing either 20% or 25%.

The US Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed tariffs together with extensive reports of how each jurisdiction's trade practices purportedly impact American commerce.

The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year and have to go through rounds of public consultation and, potentially, hearings.

Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of a good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing products.

Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.

The proposed tariffs will affect goods from China, the European Union, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Japan, and India.

The USTR's Jamieson Greer said the latest tariffs issued would "level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy".

He said that many of America's trading partners had "for decades" adopted industrial strategies which included "targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression".

They also employ "other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America's manufacturing base", Greer said.

But economists have warned tariffs can fuel inflation and push prices up for consumers if businesses pass on higher costs, as well as dampen global trade.

Trump has repeatedly threatened or imposed tariffs during his second term, arguing they will boost US manufacturing and create jobs.

Despite a poor result for the Republican party in the midterm elections, the president has continued to press on with his flagship trade policy.

Trump is also seeking to cut the US trade deficit - the gap between the value of goods it buys from other countries and those it sells to them.

These new levies are build on a "stronger legal foundation" under US law compared with Trump's April 2025 Liberation Day tariffs, Singapore Management University economics lecturer Chang Pao-Li said.

Trump previously invoked emergency presidential powers to impose tariffs that have since been struck down, while his latest approach relies on the USTR's authority to impose tariffs to address certain foreign trade practices, she said.

The levies are still likely to face legal challenges, but there has been a "historical precedent" for such tariffs remaining in force, Chang said.

Many tariffs imposed under Section 301 - a law that allows the US to probe and retaliate against foreign trade practices - during Trump's first term remained in effect during his successor Joe Biden's administration.

However, Stephen Brown, chief North America economist for Capital Economics, said the latest tariff announcement was "not as alarming as it looks", due to the taxes "essentially replacing" previously announced tariffs made in the summer.

"The increase in the effective tariff rate looks set to be a touch lower than we've been assuming for our forecasts, although the new tariffs will still provide a marginal boost to prices," he said in a note.

The additional tariff burden is likely to be small because a limited number of goods are subject to the new duties, Brown added.

Jurisdictions affected by the new wave of tariffs have voiced their disapproval over the Trump administration's move.

Washington has also proposed a 10% tariff on goods from Brazil, as part of a separate investigation over what it says are "harmful trade practices" undercutting American workers.

Brazilian authorities expressed their "outrage" at the announcement, saying that the move is aimed at pressuring the government to change regulations around issues like digital trade.

The South American nation faces duties on finished aircraft and sugar sold to the US.

"Brazil will not yield to such threats," President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's office said.

The European Commission rejected the new US tariffs, saying it would investigate the reasons for bringing them in. It pointed out that tariffs are limited to the 15% previously agreed.

The latest tariff rate is "not consistent" with the reality of bilateral economic-trade cooperation between the US and Vietnam, Vietnamese Deputy Prime Minister Bui Thanh Son said.

The Japanese government said the US tariffs were "regrettable", while the Singapore government said it disagrees with the White House's findings and that it is engaging the USTR to explore ways to reduce the tariff.

South Korea's trade minister said the proposed 15% tariff will be "more than a decent outcome" as it would fall in line with a previously agreed limit with Washington.

Last year, Seoul pledged $350bn (£267bn) in US investments in exchange for lower tariffs as part of a trade deal.

US trading partners have been "waiting for this shoe to drop" and have argued that they are being wrongly accused of producing too much, said the Asia Society Policy Institute's Wendy Cutler, a former senior US trade negotiator.

"Many believe that China, not them, should be the target for US action," she added.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun described the new tariffs as a form of "political manipulation", describing as "false" the US claim that China produces more than it can consume.

The tariff announcement is likely to increase tensions between the US and China, the world's two biggest economies, who remain locked in a trade dispute and the AI race.

The two countries have also been embroiled in a tit-for-tat tariffs war, which is currently on hold.

Despite last week's meeting between Trump and China's President Xi Jinping, the two sides made no announcement on the trade war truce, which is set to expire on 10 January.

Beijing has remained vague on how it will respond but for now seems "prepared to live with the new rates provided they don't exceed 20%", Cutler said.

Trump administration pays back $100bn in 'Liberation Day' tariffs to businesses

items.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather
items.summary: The move represents the first postponement of the iconic event, and comes after a forecast of strong winds and heavy rain.
items.content:
Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of severe weather.

Preparations to hold the iconic holiday celebration, known for its massive balloons that float among the city's skyscrapers, had already begun when the forecast for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday led to the delay.

The parade was suspended was during World War Two, but it has never before been postponed due to weather. In 1971, Macy's decided to ground the balloons, which often feature beloved characters from pop culture, because of weather.

A powerful coastal storm is set to affect the New York area in coming days.

On Wednesday night, New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a state of emergency for Long Island, New York City and Westchester County.

The potent nor'easter is expected to make it too windy and dangerous for the iconic balloons to fly.

Macy's had expected to put 100 inflatables into the sky to mark its 100th parade and feature 10 new balloons, including one depicting the animated dog Bluey wearing a crown and another showing a Minion character riding a banana like a horse.

"While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants and spectators is, and always will be, our top priority," said Will Cross, the parade's executive producer, during a news conference on Wednesday with city officials.

Cross also said the giant balloons would be deflated on Wednesday night and stored at a facility in neighbouring New Jersey until they were reinflated for the parade on Saturday.

Macy's confirmed the new parade date and updated a countdown clock on its website to reflect the Saturday schedule. Meanwhile, broadcaster NBC has said it will show the 2025 parade on Thursday.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who will not attend the parade on Saturday because of a scheduled surgery, said at the news conference that "you have to plan for every possibility" and confirmed that "extreme weather has forced" officials to make the change.

"We know that this is an inconvenience for many who come to visit our city. This decision, however, was made with safety being paramount," he said. "We want to ensure that we're delivering a parade that's not only incredible and spectacular, but one also that doesn't come at the expense of anyone's safety."

Mamdani also said that there would be an expanded police presence along the parade route on Saturday and that there were "no known specific or credible threats to the parade at this time".

Cross added that Macy's is working through what costs it could cover as a result of the delay and said the company is in contact with bands, performers and others who travelled to the city for the parade.

During some past parades, strong winds and inclement weather have led to the tearing and deflation of the balloons as well as collisions with lampposts that caused injuries.

The US National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning, valid from 10:00 local time (15:00 GMT) on Thursday until 01:00 (06:00 GMT) on Friday with gusts potentially reaching 60mph (97km/h) - although the very strongest winds are likely to occur after the parade was due to end.

Heavy rain and coastal flooding will pose additional hazards across the eastern US as the storm sweeps through, while some inland parts could also see snow, BBC Weather reports.

The governor of the neighbouring state of New Jersey on Wednesday declared a state of emergency across the state's 21 counties, beginning at 18:00 local time (23:00 GMT).

Governor Mikie Sherrill's office said the powerful coastal storm is expected to bring damaging winds, heavy rainfall, and severe tidal flooding through Friday, with coastal and bayside communities facing the greatest risk. Sherrill urged residents to stay off the roads as much as possible once the storm arrives.

Originally called the Macy's Christmas Parade, the celebration, which also features live performers, debuted in 1924 as a way to boost holiday sales. It was founded by Macy's employees and their families.

From 1942 to 1944 New York went without the parade as the US directed materials like rubber and helium toward the country's war effort.

The 2.5mi (4km) procession route begins at Macy's Herald Square flagship store and concludes in Manhattan's Upper West Side, with performers and spectators lining the streets to greet Santa Claus and ring in the holiday season.

Country artist Megan Moroney and Grammy nominee Teddy Swims were slated to perform at the flagship store, but it is unclear whether they, along with the dozens of celebrities and float performers on the roster, would be returning on Saturday.

New York's annual Thanksgiving Parade threatened by approaching storm

Storms targeting both US coasts threaten to snarl Thanksgiving travel for millions

items.title: Qualcomm's Oryon 3 Reaches the Top
items.summary: Article URL: https://chipsandcheese.com/p/qualcomms-oryon-3-reaches-the-top Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50651158 Points: 63 # Comments: 30
items.content:
Qualcomm’s laptop effort had humble beginnings. Their early Arm-based laptops used cell phone SoCs, and suffered from noticeably poor performance even against lower end Intel chips. But breaking into the PC market was going to be a marathon rather than a sprint, and Qualcomm has been persistent. Qualcomm created higher performance Snapdragon variants targeted at laptops, which became increasingly competent with each generation. Now, Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme can deliver CPU performance that challenges the best of its x86-64 competition. To deliver that performance, Qualcomm relies on the third generation of their in-house Oryon architecture, which I’ll call Oryon 3 for short.

The Snapdragon X2 Elite deploys Oryon 3 in both E-Core and P-Core variants, which Qualcomm confusingly calls “performance” and “prime” cores, respectively. P-Cores are the star of the show in the Snapdragon X2 Elite, where they provide both maximum single threaded performance while also providing the bulk of multithreaded throughput. That’s because Qualcomm has P-Cores outnumber their E-Cores by a factor of two, creating an inverted hybrid strategy compared to Intel’s. Thanks to this strategy, Qualcomm’s Oryon 3 P-Core variant shoulders most of the burden when it comes to Qualcomm’s PC market ambitions.

Oryon 3 takes on this burden by deploying an architecture with a strong resemblance to the first Oryon generation. Qualcomm technically has a second generation Oryon core, but only used it in phones. Their website also suggests it’s a very minor change over the first generation, so I’ll be treating first generation Oryon as Oryon 3’s direct predecessor.

Similarity to Oryon 1 is a good thing, because that gives Oryon 3 just about everything you could ask for from a 2026-era high performance design. From Oryon 1, Oryon 3 inherits an out-of-order window in excess of 600 micro-ops. Qualcomm has also carried forward a two-level cache setup that emphasizes speed over capacity. Compared to its predecessor, Oryon 3 takes things up a notch by pushing clock speeds to 5 GHz. It’s a huge 16% increase over the 4.3 GHz speed that Oryon 1 could reach, and is enough to offer a generational performance gain on its own. But Qualcomm doesn’t stop there. Oryon 3 increases core width to 9 micro-ops, up from 8 in its predecessor, and makes a number of improvements throughout the pipeline. Qualcomm brings SVE2 and SME support to the new core as well, keeping it up-to-date with the evolving aarch64 architecture and opening up new software optimization opportunities. In its role as a maximum performance architecture, Oryon 3 faces off against the likes of AMD’s Zen 5 and Intel’s Lion Cove. Arm’s Cortex X925 is another competitor, thanks to Nvidia’s laptop push with N1X.

Setting aside clock speed, Oryon 3’s headline architectural improvement is a core width increase from 8 to 9 ups. At the frontend, Qualcomm supports this by adding another decode slot. The fetch and decode pipeline otherwise looks mostly unchanged. Oryon 1 already had over-provisioned instruction cache bandwidth at 64 bytes per cycle, which is more than sufficient to feed a 8-wide or 9-wide aarch64 decoder. Qualcomm has also kept a 192 KB, 6-way instruction cache with hardware coherency, as well as a 256 entry 8-way instruction TLB. These large structures should help the core use its fastest instruction delivery path more often than its peers, which have smaller instruction caches and instruction TLBs. Impressively, Qualcomm managed to keep these large structures and add an extra decode slot while keeping a 13 cycle branch mispredict penalty. Clock speed increases often come with compromises like longer pipelines or smaller structures, but here Qualcomm is able to have their cake and eat it too.

Testing instruction bandwidth with a stream of NOPs validates the increased decoder width when the test loop fits within the instruction cache. Improvements continue at larger instruction footprints. Oryon 3 is able to sustain about 4 NOPs/cycle from L2, compared to 2 per cycle on Oryon 1. Qualcomm might have changed something with instruction prefetching from L2, or they might have widened datapaths between the instruction cache and L2. Whatever the case, Oryon 3 now matches the likes of AMD’s Zen 5 and Intel’s Lion Coves in terms of streaming code from L2, while boasting a much larger L2. AMD and Intel’s cores do have a L3 that provides more capacity than Qualcomm’s L2, but fetching code from that L3 will cause another drop in instruction throughput.

High core throughput places pressure on the branch predictor, which must follow the instruction stream fast enough to keep the core fed. Oryon 3 improves by expanding its predecessor’s ability to handle taken branches back-to-back. Oryon 1 could only do “zero-bubble” taken branches within a 8 KB instruction footprint. Oryon 3 can do so within a 2048 branch footprint, regardless of branch spacing and code footprint. Perhaps Qualcomm switched to using a fully decoupled 2048 entry BTB. Realistically, that means Oryon 3 should be able to do zero-bubble taken branches over a branch footprint 2x to 4x larger than its predecessor, considering typical branch spacing.

Compared to AMD and Intel’s latest cores, Qualcomm lacks any ability to handle more than one taken branch per cycle. Arm’s newer cores are also capable of doing two taken branches per cycle. I suspect AMD, Arm, and Intel decided that handling multiple taken branches per cycle became more profitable once their cores got wide enough, so seeing Qualcomm build a very wide core without that ability is surprising. Perhaps clock speed factors into that decision, because going from 4.3 to 5 GHz is a huge jump. If so, Qualcomm’s choice would be justified because a clock speed increase of that magnitude probably offers a larger performance increase than going for two taken branches per cycle. Of course, it’s impossible to know if branch predictor paths presented a timing challenge for Oryon.

For branches with dynamic taken/not-taken behavior, Oryon 3 has a 2-cycle conditional predictor. Testing with branches whose outcomes correlate with increasingly long history lengths shows an average 0.5 cycle increase in time per branch over an always- taken reference run, as long as the test stays within the conditional predictor’s capabilities. Because I randomly generate patterns so that each branch is taken roughly 50% of the time, a 0.5 cycle average penalty suggests Qualcomm only incurs the 2-cycle timing if the direction predictor disagrees with a base prediction. Direction prediction starts falling apart with more than 32K patterns in play, which is an improvement over the approximately 24K patterns that first generation Oryon could handle in this test.

For comparison, Zen 5’s conditional predictor can handle roughly 48K patterns before falling apart. Unlike Oryon 3, and unlike some older Zen generations, Zen 5 does not show an increase in branch latency compared to an always-taken pattern.

Indirect branches can go to multiple targets, and present another level of difficulty because the branch predictor has to select between previously seen targets, and must store more than one target per branch. Oryon 3 has a 2-cycle indirect predictor that can track 2048 indirect targets, matching its predecessor.

A single branch can jump to 256 targets without incurring a significant penalty. This could mean at least eight of the bits that Oryon 3 uses to index into its indirect target array are influenced by branch history.

A 50 entry return stack handles return predictions, just as on Oryon 1. However, testing shows that Oryon 3 can use all 50 entries before hitting a performance degradation. When call depth exceeds return stack capacity, Oryon 3 degrades gracefully rather than immediately taking a drastic penalty as Oryon 1 does. Oryon 1’s performance drop is heavy enough to suggest it’s mispredicting every return after the return stack overflows.

Perhaps Qualcomm implemented a new mechanism to keep a single overflow from messing up the entire return stack, and lets Oryon 3 only mispredict returns whose addresses get forced out on an overflow. Whatever this optimization is, it gives Oryon 3 return prediction behavior in-line with many other cores, including AMD’s Zen 5 and Intel’s Skymont. In capacity terms, AMD’s Zen 5 has a slightly larger 52 entry return stack.

Optimizations at the rename and allocate stage on Qualcomm’s big core are remarkably similar to those on its little core counterpart . Both cores can eliminate up to two register-to-register MOVs per cycle. They can also eliminate up to two add-immediate instructions, as long as their immediates sum to 255 or less. It’s slightly strange that Qualcomm has kept the same optimization capability even though the big core is more than twice as wide as its little core companion. That results in degraded microbenchmark figures when I chain dependent MOVs or add-immediate instructions without a break, because the wider core can get more of those instructions into the same rename group, which means the two-per-cycle restriction causes more missed optimization opportunities.
